audit_findings.title: Negative-anchor growth reverses the scenario economics
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $532 million equity-value inversion, or $23.68 per share, between BEAR and BULL
audit_findings.mechanism: growth rates applied to negative anchor OE make higher assumed growth enlarge losses throughout the forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Management’s assumptions included a truckload market recovery beginning in early-2027, which was previously estimated to begin mid-2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling error: BULL produces a value of negative $66.09 per share versus negative $42.41 for BEAR. Management's expected 2027 recovery further shows that the scenarios do not represent their stated economics. A normalized recovery path could materially change or invalidate the published valuation outputs, although its value cannot be quantified from the record.
audit_findings.action: Replace percentage growth from negative OE with filed-evidence-based loss, recovery, and normalized mid-cycle OE paths; otherwise retain the too-hard conclusion and withdraw the numerical values.

audit_findings.title: FleetNet contradicts the null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.mechanism: FleetNet earnings, disposal gain, and sale proceeds may affect historical OE and the comparability of the series used to judge growth and cyclicality
audit_findings.evidence: On February 28, 2023, the Company sold FleetNet America, Inc. (“FleetNet”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, for an aggregate adjusted cash purchase price of $100.9 million, including post-closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing confirms a $100.9 million sale and states that FleetNet was retrospectively excluded from periods presented, but it does not establish that every 2016-2022 OE observation was rebuilt on that basis. The possible OE distortion is not the sale price and cannot be quantified from the supplied record. Current 2025 anchor OE is unaffected, but a mixed historical perimeter could alter normalization and the too-hard assessment.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2022 OE from continuing-operations figures that exclude FleetNet, and reconcile discontinued earnings, the disposal gain, and $100.9 million of proceeds so each is excluded or recognized exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The reinvestment perimeter can omit capitalized software
audit_findings.magnitude: filed capitalized software of $13.391 million in 2025, $16.897 million in 2024, and $12.977 million in 2023; earlier-year treatment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: omitting capitalized software or financed equipment from maintenance capex understates reinvestment and overstates OE
audit_findings.evidence: Depreciation and amortization expense includes amortization of internally developed capitalized software which has not been included in gross capital expenditures presented in the table.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that internally developed software is outside the disclosed gross-capex table. It does not demonstrate whether the valuation separately deducted that investment. The 2025 software amount equals 12.7% of the absolute $105.3 million anchor, while the historical and maintenance-versus-growth classifications remain unresolved. The filed gross-capex table already includes $117.855 million of 2025 equipment financed through notes, but the valuation's actual treatment must still be reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to the separate software-capitalization cash-flow line and gross economic capex including financed equipment, then rerun OE using a documented maintenance-reinvestment classification.

audit_findings.title: A pension withdrawal claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $17.511 million liability at 2026-06-30, equal to computed $0.78 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: the liability is a claim ahead of common equity unless its principal-like cash settlements are already retained in OE
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the outstanding withdrawal liability recognized in the consolidated balance sheet for this obligation totaled $17.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is a real bridge or cash-flow reconciliation issue, but the recorded claim is only about 0.6% of the computed $3.168 billion market capitalization at the valuation price. A full bridge deduction would reduce value by approximately $0.78 per share and cannot change the current negative-value conclusion. Additional liabilities from future restructurings or withdrawals are contingent and unquantified rather than present adjustments.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.6 million annual settlement payments through OE and either retain those payments in OE or deduct the $17.511 million liability once; monitor and separately quantify any withdrawal exposure triggered by the proposed site closures.

audit_findings.title: Self-insurance reserve error could materially distort OE
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $12.2 million pre-tax expense sensitivity for a 10% increase in estimated IBNR
audit_findings.mechanism: reserve inadequacy would understate claims expense, overstate OE, and leave an understated liability ahead of equity
audit_findings.evidence: A 10% increase in the estimate of IBNR would increase the total 2025 expense for workers’ compensation and third-party casualty claims by approximately $12.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: No reserve error is demonstrated: the filing says payments have been reasonable relative to estimates, and the auditor tested the reserve as a critical audit matter. Nevertheless, the $12.2 million sensitivity equals 11.6% of the absolute 2025 anchor OE, and the record does not establish whether adverse development is temporary, recurring, or already captured. Materiality therefore remains unresolved rather than proven.
audit_findings.action: Prepare accident-year reserve-development triangles through the June 2026 quarter, reconcile paid and incurred severity, quantify effects of higher retention limits, and rerun OE only for demonstrated adverse development beyond booked reserves.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 property-sale gain may be recurring in the anchor or counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $15.7 million pre-tax or $11.8 million after-tax gain ($0.51 per diluted share); filed total 2025 asset-sale proceeds were $34.470 million, with exact overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: retaining the gain in net income and also netting related proceeds against capex would increase OE twice
audit_findings.evidence: Consolidated operating results benefited from the sale of certain properties, including two former service center locations, during the third quarter of 2025, which resulted in a net gain of $15.7 million (pre-tax), or $11.8 million (after-tax) and $0.51 per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation does not disclose enough detail to establish either treatment error. The known after-tax gain is 11.2% of the absolute $105.3 million anchor, and even the entire filed $34.470 million of asset-sale proceeds is only a bounding scale because property-specific proceeds are not supplied. Correcting either possible error would make the already-negative anchor and valuation more negative, not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE to net income with the $11.8 million after-tax gain removed and identify the property-specific portion of sale proceeds in the capex input; retain no more than one economically appropriate disposal treatment.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed FY2023 residual D&A of $12.449 million, equal to 8.8% of filed $145.349 million D&A
audit_findings.mechanism: eligible residual D&A would be added back to 2023 OE, but it does not affect the latest-actual 2025 anchor
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $132.9m (91.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is conservative uncertainty rather than an overstatement. Even if the entire residual were eligible, 2023 OE would rise only from negative $2.7 million to approximately positive $9.7 million. The valuation remains anchored to negative $105.3 million of 2025 OE, and the extreme historical volatility and too-hard conclusion remain intact.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $12.449 million residual from filed depreciation schedules and rerun the historical series only for components demonstrated to be eligible add-backs.
